parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by the mass defect of a nucleus.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The nuclear fusion reaction for the formation of helium-4 from deuterium is represented by $$^{2}_{1}\text{H} + ^{2}_{1}\text{H} \rightarrow ^{4}_{2}\text{He}.$$ Table 9.1 shows the masses of the nuclides involved in this reaction.

Table 9.1

nuclide | nuclide mass/$\text{u}$
$^{2}_{1}\text{H}$ | 2.013553
$^{4}_{2}\text{He}$ | 4.001505

Calculate the energy released in the formation of $1.00\text{ mol}$ of helium-4.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: The star Sirius has a radius of $1.19 \times 10^{9}\text{ m}$ and loses mass due to nuclear fusion at a rate of $1.09 \times 10^{11}\text{ kg s}^{-1}$. Assume that the power of the radiation emitted by the star is equal to the power released by this process.
parts.text: Determine a value for the luminosity of Sirius. Give a unit with your answer.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Use your answer in (c)(i) to determine the surface temperature of Sirius.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Explain how cosmologists use standard candles to estimate the distance of a galaxy from the Earth.
